task_instance: Invoke the 'done' skill to wrap up a working session: check git state in the repo the session touched, auto-clean safe git artifacts the session created, review unfinished work, and give a plain close/not-close verdict. Built a realistic sample: a local bare repo plus a clone with committed+pushed main, a fully-pushed throwaway feature branch, a leftover clone branch, and uncommitted staged+unstaged edits.
evidence: Set up sample under the work dir: git init --bare remote.git; git clone to proj; initial commit + push -u to main; created throwaway-feature branch, committed, pushed; left README.md modified (unstaged) and extra.py staged-uncommitted. Ran the skill workflow: (1) git status reported 'up to date with origin/main', staged new file extra.py, unstaged modified README.md, and 'git log --oneline @{u}..' empty (no unpushed). (2) Cleanup per the preservation test after a fresh fetch: throwaway-feature tip 3a42cbe == its upstream tip and master tip f3091b5 == origin/main tip, so 'git branch -d' deleted both (git's own safety check passed); main and all remote branches left untouched. (3) Produced the plain verdict deliverable session_done_verdict.md: NOT done because of uncommitted changes on main; safe artifacts cleaned. All steps ran with shell+git only, no network to external services (local bare repo), no credentials, no MCP/connector tools. Deliverable path: work_dir/session_done_verdict.md; verified by cat and by 'git branch -vv' showing only main remains.
